title.zh: 卷四十六 列傳第三十六 李安人 戴僧靜 桓康 焦度 曹武 呂安國 周山圖 周盤龍 王廣之
title.en: Volume 46 Biographies 36: Lian Ren, Dai Sengjing, Huan Kang, Jia Du, Cao Wu, Lu Anguo, Zhou Shantu, Zhou Panlong, Wang Guangzhi
title.raw: 卷四十六 列傳第三十六 李安人 戴僧靜 桓康 焦度 曹武 呂安國 周山圖 周盤龍 王廣之 Volume 46 Biographies 36: Lian Ren, Dai Sengjing, Huan Kang, Jia Du, Cao Wu, Lu Anguo, Zhou Shantu, Zhou Panlong, Wang Guangzhi

sentences.zh: 李安人

translations.literal: Li Anren
translations.idiomatic: Li Anren

sentences.zh: 安人少有大志，常拊髀歎曰：「大丈夫處世，富貴不可希，取三將五校，何難之有。

translations.literal: From youth Anren had great ambitions; he would often slap his thigh and sigh, saying, "A great man in the world—wealth and nobility cannot be hoped for, but to attain the ranks of three generals and five colonels—what difficulty is there in that?"
translations.idiomatic: From youth Li Anren harbored grand ambitions. He would often slap his thigh and sigh: "In this world a true man cannot count on wealth and rank—but to win three generalships and five colonelcies, what could be easier?"

sentences.zh: 」隨父在縣，宋元嘉中，縣被魏克，安人尋率部曲自拔南歸。

translations.literal: " Following his father in the county, during the Yuanjia era of Song the county was captured by Wei; Anren soon led his retainers to break out and return south.
translations.idiomatic: " While he followed his father at the county seat, the Yuanjia reign saw the place taken by Wei. Li Anren soon rallied his household troops, fought his way free, and marched south to rejoin the Song court.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，稍遷武衛將軍，領水軍討晉安王子勳，所向克捷。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Ming he was gradually promoted to General of the Martial Guard and led the naval forces in campaigning against Prince Zixun of Jin'an; wherever he went he achieved swift victory.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he rose step by step to General of the Martial Guard and commanded the fleet against Prince Zixun of Jin'an, winning every battle he fought.

sentences.zh: 事平，明帝大會新亭樓，勞諸軍主。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Emperor Ming held a great banquet at the Xinting Tower to reward the army commanders.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, Emperor Ming held a grand feast on the Xinting Tower to honor the commanders.

sentences.zh: 摴蒱官賭，安人五擲皆盧。

translations.literal: The pitch-pot dice official gambled; Anren cast five times and each throw was "lu" (the highest).
translations.idiomatic: A dice-master was gambling at court; Li Anren rolled five times and each throw came up full house.

sentences.zh: 帝大驚，目安人曰：「卿面方如田，封侯相也。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly startled and looked at Anren, saying, "Your face is square as a field—clearly the physiognomy of a enfeoffed noble."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished, fixed his eyes on Li Anren, and said, "Your face is broad as a field—surely the look of a man destined for a marquisate."

sentences.zh: 」安人少時貧，有一人從門過，相之。

translations.literal: When Anren was young and poor, a man passed by his door and read his physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: In his poverty as a young man, a stranger passing his door had read his features.

sentences.zh: 曰：「君後當大富貴，與天子交手共戲。

translations.literal: He said, "You will later attain great wealth and nobility and will play games hand to hand with the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The man had said, "You will one day be enormously rich and honored, and you will play games face to face with the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」至是，安人尋此人，不知所在。

translations.literal: By this time Anren sought out this man but could not find where he was.
translations.idiomatic: Now Li Anren searched for that fortune-teller, but no one knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 後為廣陵太守，行南兗州事。

translations.literal: Later he became Administrator of Guangling and acted as overseer of South Yan Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Administrator of Guangling and exercised authority over South Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝在淮陰，安人遙相結事。

translations.literal: When the Qi Emperor Gao was at Huaiyin, Anren from afar entered into alliance with him.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Gao of Qi was still at Huaiyin, Li Anren sought him out from a distance and pledged his support.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，除司州刺史，領義陽太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhui era he was appointed Inspector of Si Province and concurrently Administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanhui reign he was named Inspector of Si Province and also held the post of Administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 及桂陽王休范起事，安人遣軍援都。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rose in rebellion, Anren sent troops to aid the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, Li Anren dispatched forces to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素起兵，安人破其軍于葛橋。

translations.literal: When Prince Jingsu of Jianping raised troops, Anren routed his army at Ge Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingsu of Jianping took up arms; Li Anren destroyed his force at Ge Bridge.

sentences.zh: 景素誅，留安人行南徐州事。

translations.literal: After Jingsu was executed, Anren was retained to oversee South Xu Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jingsu had been put to death, Li Anren was left in charge of South Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 城局參軍王回素為安人所親，盜絹二匹。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, a staff officer of the city bureau whom Anren favored, stole two bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, a bureau staff officer whom Li Anren had long favored, stole two bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 安人流涕謂曰：「我與卿契闊備嘗，今日犯王法，乃卿負我也。

translations.literal: Anren wept and said to him, "You and I have shared every hardship; today you have violated the royal law—it is you who have failed me."
translations.idiomatic: Li Anren wept and told him, "We have been through everything together; by breaking the law today you are the one who has betrayed our bond."

sentences.zh: 」於軍門斬之，厚為斂祭，軍府皆震服。

translations.literal: " He had him beheaded at the army gate, gave him a lavish funeral, and the entire headquarters trembled in submission.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Wang Hui executed at the camp gate, then buried him with full honors. Every office in the command submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 轉東中郎司馬，行會稽郡事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Eastern Staff Major and acted as overseer of Kuaiji commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Eastern Staff Major and governed Kuaiji commandery in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 時蒼梧縱虐，齊高帝憂迫無計。

translations.literal: At that time the Cangwu emperor ran wild in cruelty, and Emperor Gao of Qi was pressed with worry and had no plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Cangwu emperor was then raging in tyranny, and Emperor Gao of Qi, desperate and without a strategy,

sentences.zh: 安人白高帝，欲于東奉江夏王躋起兵。

translations.literal: Anren told the Emperor Gao that he wished to raise troops in the east under Prince Ji of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Anren urged Emperor Gao to proclaim Prince Ji of Jiangxia in the east and march against the throne.

sentences.zh: 高帝不許，乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gao did not consent, and so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao refused, and the plan went no further.

sentences.zh: 子元履，幼有操業，甚閑政體，為司徒竟陵王子良法曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Yuanlü, from childhood possessed moral conduct and was thoroughly versed in administrative forms; he served as Legal Bureau Attendant to the Prince of Jingling, the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanlü showed discipline from boyhood and a keen grasp of government procedure; he served as Legal Bureau Attendant to Prince Ziliang of Jingling, the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 與王融遊狎，及王融誅，郁林敕元履隨右衛將軍王廣之北征，密令於北殺之。

translations.literal: He associated closely with Wang Rong; when Wang Rong was executed, Emperor Yulin ordered Yuanlü to follow the Right Guard General Wang Guangzhi on the northern campaign, secretly instructing him to kill Yuanlü in the north.
translations.idiomatic: He was intimate with Wang Rong; after Wang Rong's execution, Emperor Yulin ordered Yuanlü to accompany Right Guard General Wang Guangzhi northward, secretly commanding that he be killed on the road.

sentences.zh: 廣之先為安人所厚，又知元履無過，甚擁護之。

translations.literal: Guangzhi had earlier been greatly favored by Anren and knew Yuanlü was guiltless, so he protected him zealously.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangzhi had once owed much to Li Anren and knew Yuanlü was innocent, so he shielded him with all his might.

sentences.zh: 會郁林敗死，元履拜謝廣之，曰：「二十二載，父母之年，自此以外，丈人之賜也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yulin fell and died, Yuanlü bowed in thanks to Guangzhi and said, "Twenty-two years—the years of my parents; beyond that, it is the gift of my elder."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin met his downfall, Yuanlü thanked Wang Guangzhi and said, "Twenty-two years—the span my parents might have wished for me; anything beyond that I owe to you, sir."

sentences.zh: 」仕梁為吳郡太守，度支尚書，衡、廣、青、冀四州刺史。

translations.literal: " He served Liang as Administrator of Wu commandery, Minister of Revenue, and Inspector of the four provinces Heng, Guang, Qing, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: " Under Liang he rose to Administrator of Wu commandery, Minister of Revenue, and Inspector of Heng, Guang, Qing, and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: 戴僧靜

translations.literal: Dai Sengjing
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sengjing

sentences.zh: 戴僧靜，會稽永興人也。

translations.literal: Dai Sengjing was a native of Yongxing in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sengjing came from Yongxing in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 少有膽力，便弓馬。

translations.literal: From youth he had courage and strength and was skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and powerful and excelled at archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 事刺史沈文秀，俱被魏虜，後將家屬叛還淮陰。

translations.literal: He served Inspector Shen Wenxiu and together they were captured by the Wei invaders; later he led his household in rebellion back to Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Inspector Shen Wenxiu until both were taken by the Wei; later he brought his family in flight back to Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝撫畜，常在左右。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi nurtured him and kept him constantly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi took him in and kept him always near at hand.

sentences.zh: 後於都私齎錦出，事發，系南兗州獄。

translations.literal: Later in the capital he privately carried brocade out for sale; the matter came to light and he was imprisoned in the South Yan provincial jail.
translations.idiomatic: Later in the capital he was caught smuggling brocade for sale and was thrown into the South Yan provincial prison.

sentences.zh: 高帝遣薛深餉僧靜酒食，以刀子置魚腹中。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gao sent Xue Shen to bring Sengjing food and drink, placing a knife inside a fish.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao sent Xue Shen with food and wine; a knife was hidden in the belly of a fish.

sentences.zh: 僧靜與獄吏飲酒及醉，以刀刻械，手自折鎖，髮屋而出，歸高帝。

translations.literal: Sengjing drank with the jailers until drunk, used the knife to carve the stocks, broke the locks with his own hands, tore through the roof, and came out to rejoin the Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sengjing feasted the guards until they were drunk, carved through his fetters with the knife, broke the locks himself, climbed out through the roof, and returned to Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 帝匿之齋內，以其家貧，年給穀千斛。

translations.literal: The emperor hid him in his private quarters; because his family was poor, he granted them a thousand piculs of grain each year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor concealed him in his inner quarters and, as the family was destitute, allotted them a thousand piculs of grain every year.

sentences.zh: 會魏軍至，僧靜應募出戰，單刀直前。

translations.literal: When the Wei army arrived, Sengjing volunteered for battle and advanced alone with a single blade.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei troops appeared, Dai Sengjing enlisted, charged forward with one sword,

sentences.zh: 魏軍奔退，又追斬三級。

translations.literal: The Wei army fled in retreat; he pursued and beheaded three men.
translations.idiomatic: and drove the enemy back; pursuing, he took three heads.

sentences.zh: 時天寒甚，乃脫衣，口銜三頭，拍浮而還。

translations.literal: The weather was bitterly cold; he stripped off his clothes, held the three heads in his teeth, and swam back clinging to a float.
translations.idiomatic: It was fiercely cold. He stripped, gripped the three heads between his teeth, and swam back on a float.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，高帝入朝堂，遣僧靜將腹心先至石頭經略袁粲。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, the Emperor Gao entered the audience hall and sent Sengjing with his trusted men ahead to Stone City to deal with Yuan Can.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Emperor Gao went to court and sent Dai Sengjing with his closest followers to secure Stone City against Yuan Can.

sentences.zh: 時蘇烈據倉城門，僧靜射書與烈，夜縋入城。

translations.literal: At that time Su Lie held Cangcheng Gate; Sengjing shot a letter to Lie and was lowered into the city by rope at night.
translations.idiomatic: Su Lie then held Cangcheng Gate. Dai Sengjing shot an arrow bearing a message to Lie and was hauled over the wall at night.

sentences.zh: 粲登城西南門，列燭火坐，台軍至射之，火乃滅。

translations.literal: Can mounted the southwest gate of the city, arrayed candles and sat; when the palace troops arrived and shot, the flames went out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can took the southwest gate, set out rows of candles, and sat; when the imperial troops shot, every flame died.

sentences.zh: 回登東門，其党孫曇瓘驍勇善戰，每蕩一合，輒大殺傷，官軍死者百餘人。

translations.literal: He returned to the east gate; his partisan Sun Tanxun was fierce and skilled in battle—each time he swept through a formation he inflicted heavy slaughter, and more than a hundred government soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: He went back to the east gate. His ally Sun Tanxun fought with terrifying skill: every clash left a great heap of dead, and over a hundred imperial soldiers fell.

sentences.zh: 軍主王天生殊死拒戰，故得相持。

translations.literal: The army commander Wang Tiansheng resisted with desperate valor, and thus they were able to stalemate each other.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wang Tiansheng held him off with suicidal courage, and the fight hung in balance.

sentences.zh: 自亥至醜，有流星赤色照地墜城中，僧靜率力攻倉門，手斬粲於東門，外軍燒門入。

translations.literal: From the hai hour to the chou hour a crimson meteor blazed to the ground inside the city; Sengjing led his force in assault on Cang Gate, personally beheaded Can at the east gate, and the outer army burned the gate and entered.
translations.idiomatic: From hai to chou a crimson meteor flamed down into the city. Dai Sengjing stormed Cang Gate, cut down Yuan Can with his own hand at the east gate, and the outer force burned its way in.

sentences.zh: 以功除前軍將軍、甯朔將軍。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed General of the Vanguard and General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made General of the Vanguard and General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，巴東王子響殺僚佐，武帝召僧靜使領軍向江陵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Prince Xiang of Badong killed his staff officers; Emperor Wu summoned Sengjing to lead the army toward Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 8, Prince Xiang of Badong murdered his officials. Emperor Wu ordered Dai Sengjing to take command and march on Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 僧靜面啟上曰：「巴東王年少，長史司馬捉之太急，忿不思難故耳。

translations.literal: Sengjing addressed the throne face to face, saying, "The Prince of Badong is young; the Chief Administrator and Staff Supervisor pressed him too hard, and in resentment he acted without thinking of the consequences."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sengjing spoke plainly: "Prince Xiang of Badong is young. His chief administrator and staff supervisor seized him too roughly; in anger he struck without weighing the cost."

sentences.zh: 天子兒過誤殺人，有何大罪，今急遣軍西上，人情惶懼，無所不至。

translations.literal: " When a Son of Heaven's son kills someone in a passing error, what great crime is there? Now to rush troops westward will fill every heart with panic beyond measure."
translations.idiomatic: " A son of the emperor who kills in a moment of passion—what capital crime is that? Dispatch an army west in haste and fear will spread everywhere."

sentences.zh: 臣不敢奉敕。

translations.literal: " Your servant dares not accept the command."
translations.idiomatic: " I dare not obey this order."

sentences.zh: 」上不答而心善之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not answer but inwardly approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave no reply yet was pleased in his heart.

sentences.zh: 徙廬陵王中軍司馬、高平太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Staff Major to the Prince of Luling and Administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Staff Major to the Prince of Luling and Administrator of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡壯侯。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 桓康，北蘭陵承人也。

translations.literal: Huan Kang was a native of Cheng in North Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Kang came from Cheng in North Lanling.

sentences.zh: 勇果驍悍。

translations.literal: He was brave, resolute, fierce, and formidable.
translations.idiomatic: He was courageous, fierce, and terrifying in battle.

sentences.zh: 宋大明中，隨齊高帝為軍容，從武帝在贛縣。

translations.literal: During the Daming era of Song he followed Emperor Gao of Qi as army retainer and accompanied Emperor Wu at Gan County.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaoming's Daming reign he served Emperor Gao of Qi as army retainer and followed Emperor Wu at Gan County.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，武帝起義，為郡所縶，眾皆散。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, Emperor Wu raised the righteous army and was bound by the commandery; the crowd all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu first raised arms at the opening of Taishi, the commandery seized him and his followers scattered.

sentences.zh: 康裝擔，一頭貯穆後，一頭貯文惠太子及竟陵王子良，自負置山中。

translations.literal: Kang loaded two carrying-poles—one basket held Empress Mu, the other held Crown Prince Wenhuai and Prince Ziliang of Jingling—and bore them on his shoulders into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Kang shouldered two carrying-poles: one basket held Empress Mu, the other Crown Prince Wenhuai and Prince Ziliang of Jingling, and he bore them into the hills.

sentences.zh: 及閘客蕭欣祖等四十餘人相結，破郡獄，出武帝。

translations.literal: Together with more than forty men including the gate guest Xiao Xingu, they joined forces, broke the commandery prison, and freed Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He and over forty men, among them the gate guest Xiao Xingu, broke the jail and brought Emperor Wu out.

sentences.zh: 郡追兵急，康等死戰破之。

translations.literal: The commandery pursuit was urgent; Kang and the others fought to the death and broke through.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuit from the commandery was hot; Huan Kang and his band fought to the death and smashed through.

sentences.zh: 隨武帝起兵，摧堅陷陣，膂力絕人。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in raising troops, he stormed strongpoints and shattered formations; his physical strength was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Emperor Wu, tore through defenses, and possessed strength beyond any other man.

sentences.zh: 所經村邑，恣行暴害，江南人畏之，以其名怖小兒，畫其形於寺中。

translations.literal: In every village he passed he committed outrages at will; the people of Jiangnan feared him and used his name to frighten small children, painting his likeness in temples.
translations.idiomatic: Every hamlet he entered suffered his violence. Jiangnan feared him; parents painted his figure in temples to scare children.

sentences.zh: 病瘧者寫形帖著床壁，無不立愈。

translations.literal: Malaria sufferers who copied his image and pasted it on the bed wall were all instantly cured.
translations.idiomatic: Those with malaria who posted his portrait by the bed were said to recover at once.

sentences.zh: 後除襄賁令。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Magistrate of Xiangbin.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Magistrate of Xiangbin.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休範事起，康棄縣還都就高帝。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rose, Kang abandoned his county and returned to the capital to join Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, Huan Kang quit his post and hurried to the capital to stand with Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 會事已平，除員外郎。

translations.literal: The affair was already settled; he was appointed Extraordinary Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis had passed; he received the post of Extraordinary Attendant.

sentences.zh: 元徽五年七月六日夜，少帝微行至領軍府，帝左右人曰：「一府皆眠，何不緣牆入？

translations.literal: On the night of the sixth day of the seventh month in the fifth year of Yuanhui, the Deposed Emperor made a secret nocturnal visit to the headquarters of the General-in-Chief; the emperor's attendants said, "The whole compound is asleep—why not climb the wall?"
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the seventh month, day six, Yuanhui year 5, the deposed emperor stole to the General-in-Chief's mansion. An attendant whispered, "Everyone here is asleep—why not scale the wall?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我今夕欲一處作適，待明日夜。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Tonight I mean to enjoy myself in one place; wait until tomorrow night."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, "Tonight I want one particular diversion; we will come back tomorrow night."

sentences.zh: 」康與高帝所養健兒盧荒、向黑於門間聽得其語。

translations.literal: Kang and the strong youths Lu Huang and Xiang Hei whom Emperor Gao had raised overheard their words between the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Between the gates Huan Kang listened with Lu Huang and Xiang Hei, stalwarts Emperor Gao had trained.

sentences.zh: 明旦，王敬則將帝首至，扣府門。

translations.literal: At dawn Wang Jingze arrived with the emperor's head and knocked at the mansion gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Wang Jingze came with the emperor's head and beat on the gate.

sentences.zh: 康謂是變，與荒、黑拔白刃欲出，仍隨高帝入宮。

translations.literal: Kang thought it was a mutiny; he and Huang and Hei drew bare blades to rush out, then followed Emperor Gao into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Kang thought a coup was underway; he, Huang, and Hei drew swords to charge out, then followed Emperor Gao into the palace.

sentences.zh: 高帝鎮東府，除武陵王中兵、甯朔將軍，帶蘭陵太守，常衛左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao held the Eastern Mansion he appointed Kang Central Army Major to the Prince of Wuling, General Who Pacifies the North, and concurrent Administrator of Lanling, always guarding his person.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao governed from the Eastern Mansion, he made Huan Kang Central Army Major to the Prince of Wuling, General Who Pacifies the North, and concurrent Administrator of Lanling, guarding him constantly.

sentences.zh: 高帝誅黃回，回時為南兗州，部曲數千，欲收恐為亂，召入東府，停外齋，使康數回罪，然後殺之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao executed Huang Hui, Hui was then in South Yan with several thousand retainers; fearing disorder if they were gathered in, he was summoned to the Eastern Mansion and lodged in the outer quarters; Kang was made to enumerate Hui's crimes, and then he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao put Huang Hui to death. Hui held South Yan with thousands of followers; to avoid a riot they were called to the Eastern Mansion and kept in the outer lodge while Huan Kang listed Hui's crimes—then Hui was slain.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「欲侜張，問桓康。

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying: "If you want to deceive, ask Huan Kang."
translations.idiomatic: A saying ran: "Want to play a trick? Ask Huan Kang."

sentences.zh: 」除後軍將軍、直合將軍、南濮陽太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Rear Guard, General of the Direct Guard, and Administrator of South Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General of the Rear Guard, General of the Direct Guard, and Administrator of South Puyang.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，封吳平縣侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuiping County.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 1 he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuiping.

sentences.zh: 高帝謂康曰：「卿隨我日久，未得方伯，亦當未解我意，正欲與卿先共滅虜耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao said to Kang, "You have followed me long without receiving a regional command—I suppose you still do not understand my intent; I simply wished first to destroy the barbarians together with you."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao told him, "You have served me for years without a provincial post—you may still not grasp my meaning: I meant to crush the northern enemy with you first."

sentences.zh: 」三年，魏軍動，康大破魏軍于淮陽。

translations.literal: In the third year the Wei army moved; Kang inflicted a great defeat on the Wei army at Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the Wei advanced; at Huaiyang Huan Kang routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，卒于驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Kang died while General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Huan Kang died in office as General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 焦度字文績，南安氐也。

translations.literal: Jiao Du, style Wenji, was of the Di people of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Du, courtesy name Wenji, was a Di clansman from Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 祖文珪，避難居仇池。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wen Gui fled hardship and dwelt at Chou Pool.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wen Gui, fleeing turmoil, settled at Chou Pool.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉中，裴方明平楊難當，度父明與千餘家隨居襄陽，乃立天水郡略陽縣以居之。

translations.literal: During the Yuanjia era of Song, Pei Fangming pacified Yang Nan Dang; Du's father Ming followed with more than a thousand households to settle at Xiangyang, and the Tian Shui commandery and Lüeyang County were established to house them.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's Yuanjia reign Pei Fangming subdued Yang Nan Dang. Jiao Du's father Ming moved with a thousand-odd households to Xiangyang; the court then set up Tian Shui commandery and Lüeyang County for their settlement.

sentences.zh: 度少有氣幹，便弓馬。

translations.literal: From youth Du had spirit and capacity and was skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Jiao Du had force of character and handled bow and horse with ease.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，青州刺史顏師伯出鎮，台差度領幢主送之，與魏豹皮公遇，交槊鬥，豹皮公墯地，禽其具裝馬，手殺數十人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu, when Inspector Yan Shibo went out to his post, the court assigned Du to lead the banner detachment escorting him; he encountered the Wei "Leopard-skin Duke," fought with crossed spears, the Duke fell from his horse, Du seized his full armor and horse, and with his own hand killed several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign, as Inspector Yan Shibo took up his post, Jiao Du led the escort banner. He met the Wei commander called Leopard-skin Duke, crossed spears, knocked him from the saddle, captured horse and armor, and killed dozens with his own blade.

sentences.zh: 師伯啟孝武，稱度氣力弓馬並絕人，帝召還充左右。

translations.literal: Shibo reported to Emperor Xiaowu, praising Du's strength, bow, and horse as all unmatched; the emperor summoned him back to fill his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo reported that Jiao Du's strength, archery, and horsemanship were unrivaled; the emperor recalled him to the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 見度形狀，謂師伯曰：「此真健人也。」

translations.literal: Seeing Du's physique, he said to Shibo, "This is truly a stalwart man."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Jiao Du's build, the emperor told Yan Shibo, "There is a real fighting man."

sentences.zh: 補晉安王子勳夾轂隊主，隨鎮江州。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief of the Prince of Jin'an Zixun's escort squad and followed the prince to Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief of Prince Zixun of Jin'an's escort squad and went with him to Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 子勳起兵，以度為龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: When Zixun raised troops, Du was made General of the Dragon Battleaxe.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixun rebelled, Jiao Du was named General of the Dragon Battleaxe.

sentences.zh: 為前鋒，所向無不勝。

translations.literal: As vanguard, wherever he went he was never defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the van, he was never beaten.

sentences.zh: 事敗，逃宮亭湖為賊。

translations.literal: When the cause failed he fled to Lake Gongting and became a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion collapsed he fled to Lake Gongting and turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞其勇，甚患之。

translations.literal: The court, hearing of his valor, was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The court, hearing how fierce he was, was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 使江州刺史王景文誘降之。

translations.literal: They sent Inspector Wang Jingwen of Jiang Province to entice him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Wang Jingwen of Jiang Province was sent to lure him in.

sentences.zh: 景文以為己鎮南參軍，領中軍直兵，厚待之。

translations.literal: Jingwen made him his Aide who Pacifies the South and leader of the central army's direct troops, treating him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingwen appointed him Aide who Pacifies the South and head of the central army's direct detachment, and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 隨景文還都，常在府州內。

translations.literal: Following Jingwen back to the capital, he was constantly within the headquarters and provincial offices.
translations.idiomatic: He returned with Wang Jingwen to the capital and stayed always within the command and provincial offices.

sentences.zh: 景文被害夕，度大怒，勸景文拒命，景文不從，明帝不知也。

translations.literal: On the night Jingwen was murdered, Du was furious and urged Jingwen to resist; Jingwen would not, and Emperor Ming did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: The night Wang Jingwen was killed, Jiao Du raged and urged resistance; Jingwen refused, and Emperor Ming knew nothing of Du's part.

sentences.zh: 以度武勇，補晉熙王燮防合，隨鎮夏口。

translations.literal: Because of Du's martial valor he was appointed to the Prince of Jinxi Xie's guard corps and followed the prince to garrison Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: For his fighting prowess he was attached to Prince Xie of Jinxi's guard and garrisoned Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 武陵王贊代燮為郢州，度仍留鎮，為贊前軍參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Zan of Wuling replaced Xie in E Province, Du remained on garrison duty as Zan's Forward Army Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zan of Wuling succeeded Xie in E Province; Jiao Du stayed on station as Zan's Forward Army Attendant.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，轉度中直兵。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, Du was transferred to central direct troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Jiao Du was shifted to the central direct detachment.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝又使假度輔國將軍、屯騎校尉，轉右將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi also had him act as General Who Assists the State and Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry, then transferred him to General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi further had him act as General Who Assists the State and Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry, then promoted him to General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 度容貌壯醜，皮膚若漆，質直木訥，口不能出言。

translations.literal: Du's appearance was imposing and ugly; his skin was like lacquer; his nature was plain and blunt, and he could not get words out of his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Du was powerfully built and homely, with skin dark as lacquer. Plain and tongue-tied, he could barely speak.

sentences.zh: 晉熙王夾轂主周彥與度俱在郢州，彥有左右人與度父同名，彥常呼其名使役之。

translations.literal: Prince Xie of Jinxi's escort chief Zhou Yan and Du were both in E Province; Yan had a personal attendant with the same name as Du's father, and Yan would often call that name to make him serve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yan, escort chief to Prince Xie of Jinxi, was posted in E Province with Jiao Du. Yan had a servant who shared the name of Du's father, and Yan would shout "Ming!" to order the man about.

sentences.zh: 度積忿，呵責彥曰：「汝知我諱'明'，而恒呼明，何也！」

translations.literal: Du nursed resentment and shouted at Yan, "You know my father's taboo name 'Ming,' yet you constantly call 'Ming'—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Du's anger boiled over. He berated Yan: "You know my father's name was Ming—why do you keep calling Ming?"

sentences.zh: 及在郢城，尤為沈攸之所忿。

translations.literal: While in Ying City he was especially hated by Shen Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In Ying City he earned Shen Youzhi's particular hatred.

sentences.zh: 攸之大眾至夏口，將直下都，留偏兵守郢而已。

translations.literal: Youzhi's great host reached Xiakou and was about to press straight on the capital, leaving only a detached force to hold Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's main force reached Xiakou, poised to march on the capital; only a rear guard held Ying.

sentences.zh: 度於城樓上肆言罵辱攸之，至自髮露形體穢辱之，故攸之怒，改計攻城。

translations.literal: On the city tower Du poured out abuse and insults at Youzhi, even baring himself and reviling Youzhi with obscene gestures; therefore Youzhi in anger changed his plan and assaulted the city.
translations.idiomatic: From the tower Jiao Du screamed abuse at Shen Youzhi, finally stripping and gesturing obscenely. Youzhi, enraged, abandoned his march and besieged the city instead.

sentences.zh: 度親力戰，攸之眾蒙楯將登，度令投以穢器，賊眾不能冒，後呼此樓為焦度樓。

translations.literal: Du fought in person; Youzhi's troops covered themselves with shields and were about to climb; Du ordered filth cast down, and the enemy could not advance; later they called this tower Jiao Du Tower.
translations.idiomatic: He fought hand to hand. As the enemy raised shields to scale the wall, Jiao Du had ordure hurled down; they could not climb. The tower was afterward called Jiao Du Tower.

sentences.zh: 事甯，度功居多，封東昌縣子、東宮直合將軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Du's merit was greatest; he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Dongchang and made Direct Guard General of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After peace returned, Jiao Du's credit ranked first. He was made Viscount of Dongchang and Direct Guard General of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 還都，為貴戚追敘郢城時褰露穢褻之事，其戇如此。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, the nobles pursued the story of how at Ying he had lifted his robes and acted with such foul indecency—so blunt was he.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, the great families still gossiped about how he had exposed himself at Ying—such was his rawness.

sentences.zh: 為人樸澀，欲就高帝求州，比及見，竟不涉一語。

translations.literal: By nature he was plain and dull; he wished to ask Emperor Gao for a province, but when he came before him he did not manage a single word on the subject.
translations.idiomatic: Simple and awkward, he meant to beg Emperor Gao for a provincial post, yet when they met he never broached the topic.

sentences.zh: 帝以其不閑政事，竟不用。

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing he was unskilled in government affairs, in the end did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him unfit for civil rule and gave him nothing.

sentences.zh: 後求竟陵郡，不知所以置辭，親人授之辭百餘言，度習誦數日，皆得上口。

translations.literal: Later he sought Jingling commandery but did not know how to phrase his request; kinsmen supplied him with a speech of more than a hundred words, which Du studied for several days until he could recite it fluently.
translations.idiomatic: He later sought Jingling commandery. Unable to frame a petition, relatives coached him in a speech of a hundred-odd lines; he drilled for days until it flowed.

sentences.zh: 會高帝履行石頭城，度於大眾中欲自陳，臨時卒忘所教，乃大言曰：「度啟公，度啟公，度無食。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao was inspecting Stone City, Du wished to speak before the crowd but at the last moment forgot what he had been taught and cried out loudly, "Du reports to my lord, Du reports to my lord—Du has no food."
translations.idiomatic: During an imperial tour of Stone City, Jiao Du tried to address the court in public, forgot every coached line, and blurted, "Du reports, my lord—Du reports—Du has no food!"

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「卿何憂無食。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "Why should you worry about having no food?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed. "Why fear hunger?"

sentences.zh: 」即賜米百斛。

translations.literal: He immediately granted a hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He granted a hundred piculs of grain on the spot.

sentences.zh: 建元四年，乃除淮陵太守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyuan he was at last appointed Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Jianyuan year 4 was he named Administrator of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 性好酒，醉輒暴怒，上常使人節之。

translations.literal: He loved wine by nature; drunk he would fly into violent rage, and the emperor often sent men to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: He drank heavily; in his cups he turned savage, and the throne repeatedly sent men to curb him.

sentences.zh: 年雖老而氣力如故，除遊擊將軍，卒。

translations.literal: Though old in years his strength was as before; he was appointed General Who Roams in Attack and died.
translations.idiomatic: Age did not sap his strength. He was made General Who Roams in Attack, then died.

sentences.zh: 武形幹甚毅，善於誘納。

translations.literal: Wu was imposing in bearing and very stern, skilled at winning men over.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wu was imposing in build, stern in manner, and skilled at winning loyalty.

sentences.zh: 晚節在雍州，致見錢七千萬，皆厚輪大郭，他物稱是，馬八百匹。

translations.literal: In his later years in Yong Province he amassed cash on hand to seventy million, all in thick-rimmed large coins; other goods matched this scale, and eight hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life, as governor of Yong Province, he piled up seventy million in cash—all thick-rimmed "large belly" coins—plus comparable stores of goods and eight hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 僕妾蔬食，膳無膏腴。

translations.literal: His servants and concubines ate plain food; their meals had no rich fare.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his servants and concubines ate plainly, without rich food on the table.

sentences.zh: 嘗為梅蟲兒、茹法珍設女伎，金翠曜眼，器服精華，蟲兒等因是欲誣而奪之。

translations.literal: Once he set up female performers for Mei Chong'er and Ru Fazhen; gold and kingfisher feathers dazzled the eye and vessels and robes were splendid; Chong'er and the others therefore wished to frame him and seize his goods.
translations.idiomatic: He once entertained the favorites Mei Chong'er and Ru Fazhen with courtesans in gold and jade finery. They plotted to frame him and seize his wealth.

sentences.zh: 人傳武每好風景，輒開庫招拍張武戲。

translations.literal: People said that whenever Wu took a fancy to the scenery he would open his treasury and invite men to pitch-pot and martial games.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor had it that whenever the view pleased him, Cao Wu opened his vaults for drinking games and martial sport.

sentences.zh: 帝疑武舊將領，兼利其財，新除未及拜，遇誅。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected Wu as an old army commander and coveted his wealth; the new appointment had not yet been accepted when he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected this old commander and coveted his riches. Before the new post could be taken up, Cao Wu was put to death.

sentences.zh: 及收兵至，歎曰：「諸人知我無異意，所以殺我，政欲取吾財貨伎女耳。

translations.literal: When the arresting troops arrived he sighed, "You all know I had no other intent; you kill me simply to take my wealth and singing girls."
translations.idiomatic: As soldiers closed in he sighed, "You know I meant no treason—you kill me only for my money and women."

sentences.zh: 恨令眾輩見之。

translations.literal: " I regret letting the crowd see this."
translations.idiomatic: " I regret only that the rabble will witness it."

sentences.zh: 」諸子長成者皆見誅，唯子世宗兄弟三人未冠，系尚方，梁武帝兵至得免。

translations.literal: All sons who had come of age were executed; only his son Shizong and two brothers, not yet capped, were held at the Imperial Workshop and escaped when Emperor Wu of Liang's army arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Grown sons were all killed. Shizong and two younger brothers, still minors, were sent to the Imperial Workshop and survived when Liang forces arrived.

sentences.zh: 武雖武士，頗有知人鑒。

translations.literal: Though Wu was a military man, he had considerable discernment of men.
translations.idiomatic: For all his soldier's trade, Cao Wu read men well.

sentences.zh: 梁武及崔慧景之在襄陽，于時崔方貴盛，武性儉嗇，無所餉遺，獨饋梁武，謂曰：「卿必大貴，我當不及見，今以弱子相托。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang and Cui Huijing were at Xiangyang, Cui Fang was then in full power; Wu was frugal by nature and gave nothing to others, but only presented gifts to the future Emperor Wu, telling him, "You will surely attain great honor; I shall not live to see it—now I entrust my young son to you."
translations.idiomatic: When the future Liang emperor and Cui Huijing were at Xiangyang, Cui Fang ruled the hour. Frugal, Cao Wu courted no one but the future emperor, saying, "You will rise very high—I shall not see it. I entrust my young son to you."

sentences.zh: 」每密送錢物並好馬。

translations.literal: He secretly sent money, goods, and fine horses each time.
translations.idiomatic: He sent money, goods, and fine horses in secret, again and again.

sentences.zh: 時帝在戎多乏，就武換借，未嘗不得，遂至十七萬。

translations.literal: At that time the future emperor was often short on campaign funds and borrowed from Wu by exchange, never failing to obtain what he needed, until the sum reached one hundred seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The future emperor, often broke on campaign, borrowed from Cao Wu and was never refused, until the debt reached one hundred seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，忘其惠。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne he forgot this kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, he forgot the debt.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，帝忽夢如田塍下行，兩邊水深無底，夢中甚懼。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian the emperor suddenly dreamed he was walking along a field ridge with deep water bottomless on both sides; in the dream he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 2 he dreamed he walked a field path with bottomless water on either side and was terrified.

sentences.zh: 忽見武來負，武帝得過，曰：「卿今為天下主，乃爾忘我顧托之言邪？

translations.literal: Suddenly he saw Wu come and carry him across; the Emperor Wu got through and said, "You are now lord of all under Heaven—yet you forget the words of my entrustment?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wu appeared, carried him over, and said, "You rule the realm—yet you forget what I asked of you?"

sentences.zh: 我兒饑寒無依，昔所換十七萬，可還其市宅。

translations.literal: " My sons hunger and shiver without support; the former exchange of one hundred seventy thousand—return it for a house in the market quarter."
translations.idiomatic: " My sons are cold and hungry. Repay the one hundred seventy thousand and buy them a house."

sentences.zh: 」帝覺，即使主書送錢還之，使用市宅。

translations.literal: The emperor awoke and immediately sent the chief clerk with money to repay it and purchase the market residence.
translations.idiomatic: He woke and at once sent the chief clerk with cash to settle the debt and buy the house.

sentences.zh: 子世澄、世宗並蒙抽擢，三二年間，疊為大郡。

translations.literal: His sons Shicheng and Shizong were both promoted in turn; within two or three years they held great commanderies one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Shicheng and Shizong were raised in quick succession to govern major commanderies within a few years.

sentences.zh: 世宗性嚴明，頗識兵勢，末遂封侯富顯。

translations.literal: Shizong was stern and clear-minded and understood military affairs well, but in the end did not receive enfeoffment and great wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was strict and clear-sighted and knew warfare, yet never won a marquisate or lasting glory.

sentences.zh: 歷位太子左衛率，卒，贈左散騎常侍、左衛將軍，諡曰壯侯。

translations.literal: He held the post of Left Guard of the Heir Apparent, died, and was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant, Left Guard General, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left Guard of the Heir Apparent, died, and was posthumously named Left Regular Attendant and Left Guard General, with the title Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 呂安國

translations.literal: Lu Anguo
translations.idiomatic: Lu Anguo

sentences.zh: 安國欣有文授，謂其子曰：「汝後勿袴褶驅使，單衣猶恨不稱，當為朱衣官也。

translations.literal: Anguo was pleased that his son had literary attainments and told him, "Hereafter do not serve as a driver in trousers and jacket; even in single robes I still regret they do not fit—you ought to become an official in vermilion robes."
translations.idiomatic: Anguo rejoiced that his son had learning and told him, "Never again drive in military dress. Plain robes barely suit you—you are meant for vermilion court robes."

sentences.zh: 」曆都官尚書，太子左率，領軍將軍。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of the Court for the Nobility, Left Leader of the Heir Apparent, and General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Minister of the Court for the Nobility, Left Leader of the Heir Apparent, and General-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 安國累居將率，在朝以宿舊見遇。

translations.literal: Anguo repeatedly held command posts and in court was treated with honor as an elder of long service.
translations.idiomatic: Long a field commander, he was honored at court as an elder of the founding generation.

sentences.zh: 尋遷散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，給扶。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Regular Attendant, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with support staff granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with attendants to lean on.

sentences.zh: 永明八年卒，諡肅侯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming he died and received the posthumous title Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongming year 8 and was posthumously titled Marquis Su.

sentences.zh: 周山圖

translations.literal: Zhou Shantu
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shantu

sentences.zh: 周山圖，字季寂，義興義鄉人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Shantu, style Jiji, was a native of Yixiang in Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shantu, courtesy name Jiji, came from Yixiang in Yixing commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世寒賤，年十五六，氣力絕眾，食噉恒兼數人。

translations.literal: His family for generations was poor and low; at fifteen or sixteen his strength surpassed all others, and at meals he constantly ate for several men.
translations.idiomatic: His line was poor for generations. At fifteen or sixteen his strength outmatched everyone; at table he ate for several men.

sentences.zh: 鄉里獵戲集聚，常為主帥，指麾處分皆見從。

translations.literal: When the village gathered for hunting games he was always commander; his orders in directing and assigning were all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: In village hunts he always commanded; men obeyed his orders.

sentences.zh: 不事產業，恒願為將，雖勇健而不閑弓馬。

translations.literal: He did not attend to property; he constantly wished to be a general; though brave and strong he was not skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: He neglected estates and longed only for a general's career. Brave as he was, bow and saddle were not his gifts.

sentences.zh: 於書題甚拙，謹直少言，不嚐說人短長。

translations.literal: In writing he was very clumsy; honest and straight, he spoke little and never spoke of others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote poorly, spoke little, and never gossiped about others' failings.

sentences.zh: 與人周旋，皆白首不異。

translations.literal: In dealings with people he was the same from white hair to white hair.
translations.idiomatic: With everyone he dealt the same way from youth to old age.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉二十七年，魏軍至瓜步，台符取健兒，山圖應募，領白衣隊主。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia of Song the Wei army reached Guabu; the court talisman summoned stalwart men; Shantu volunteered and led a white-robed squad chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Song Yuanjia year 27 the Wei reached Guabu. The court called up strong men; Shantu enlisted as chief of a white-robed squad.

sentences.zh: 軍功除員外郎，加振武將軍。

translations.literal: For military merit he was appointed Extraordinary Attendant and given the additional title General Who Quells Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: For battle honors he was made Extraordinary Attendant with the additional title General Who Quells Martiality.

sentences.zh: 及鎮軍將軍張永侵魏，山圖領二千人迎運至武原，為魏軍所追，合戰多傷殺，魏軍稱其勇，呼為武原將。

translations.literal: When the General Who Pacifies the Army Zhang Yong invaded Wei, Shantu led two thousand men to meet the supply train at Wuyuan; the Wei army pursued; in the combined battle many were killed and wounded; the Wei army praised his valor and called him the General of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yong invaded Wei, Shantu led two thousand men to escort supplies to Wuyuan. Wei pursued; in the fight many fell on both sides. The enemy praised his courage and called him the Wuyuan General.

sentences.zh: 及永軍大敗，山圖收散卒，守下邳城。

translations.literal: When Yong's army suffered great defeat, Shantu gathered the scattered troops and held Xiapi city.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yong's great defeat, Shantu rallied the broken troops and held Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 還除給事中、冗從僕射、直合將軍。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace, Supernumerary Attendant of the Suite, and General of the Direct Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was then named Gentleman of the Palace, Supernumerary Attendant of the Suite, and General of the Direct Guard.

sentences.zh: 山圖好酒多失，明帝數加怒誚，後遂自改。

translations.literal: Shantu loved wine and often erred; Emperor Ming repeatedly rebuked him in anger, and afterward he reformed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He drank too much and often blundered; Emperor Ming scolded him harshly until he mended his ways.

sentences.zh: 累遷淮南太守。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 時盜發桓溫塚，大獲寶物，客竊取以遺山圖。

translations.literal: At that time robbers opened Huan Wen's tomb and obtained great treasure; a guest stole some and offered it to Shantu.
translations.idiomatic: When robbers broke open Huan Wen's tomb and took fabulous goods, a guest stole pieces and offered them to Shantu.

sentences.zh: 山圖不受，簿以還官。

translations.literal: Shantu would not accept them and registered them to return to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Shantu refused and entered every item in the register for return to the state.

sentences.zh: 遷左中郎將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Central Army Major.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Central Army Major.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝輔政，山圖密啟沈攸之久有異圖，宜為之備。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi held the regency, Shantu secretly reported that Shen Youzhi had long harbored a different design and ought to be guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: As regent, Emperor Gao of Qi received Shantu's secret report that Shen Youzhi had long plotted rebellion and must be watched.

sentences.zh: 帝笑而納之。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and took the warning to heart.

sentences.zh: 攸之事起，武帝為西討都督，啟山圖為軍副。

translations.literal: When Youzhi's affair arose, Emperor Wu was Western Campaign Commander-in-Chief and requested Shantu as army deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi rebelled, Emperor Wu commanded the western campaign and named Shantu his deputy.

sentences.zh: 攸之攻郢城，武帝令山圖量其形勢。

translations.literal: Youzhi attacked Ying City; Emperor Wu ordered Shantu to assess the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi besieged Ying; Emperor Wu asked Shantu to read the field.

sentences.zh: 山圖曰：「攸之為人，性度險刻，無以結固士心。

translations.literal: Shantu said, "Youzhi as a man is by nature harsh and cutting and cannot firmly bind the hearts of his officers."
translations.idiomatic: Shantu said, "Youzhi is harsh by nature and cannot bind his officers' loyalty."

sentences.zh: 如頓兵堅城之下，適所以為離散之漸耳。

translations.literal: " If he camps his host under a strong city, that will only hasten their scattering."
translations.idiomatic: " Pin him under a strong wall and his host will melt away."

sentences.zh: 」及攸之敗，高帝謂曰：「周公前言，可謂明於見事矣。」

translations.literal: " When Youzhi was defeated, Emperor Gao said, "Your earlier words can be called clear-sighted in reading events."
translations.idiomatic: " After Youzhi's fall, Emperor Gao said, "Your forecast showed true foresight."

sentences.zh: 轉黃門郎，領羽林監四廂直衛。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and overseer of the four wings of the Feathered Forest guard.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Attendant and commanded the four wings of the Feathered Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 山圖于新林立墅舍，晨夜往還。

translations.literal: Shantu built a villa at Xinlin and went back and forth morning and night.
translations.idiomatic: He built a villa at Xinlin and commuted there daily.

sentences.zh: 上謂曰：「卿罷萬人都督而輕行郊外，自今往墅可以仗身自隨，以備不虞。

translations.literal: The emperor said to him, "You have left command of tens of thousands yet travel lightly in the suburbs—from now when you go to the villa you may take armed escort against the unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "You quit a command of ten thousand yet stroll the suburbs alone—from now take an armed escort to your villa."

sentences.zh: 」及疾，上手敕問疾。

translations.literal: When he fell ill the emperor personally wrote to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: When illness came, the emperor wrote in his own hand to ask after him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: Soon he died at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 周盤龍

translations.literal: Zhou Panlong
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Panlong

sentences.zh: 周盤龍，北蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Panlong was a native of North Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Panlong came from North Lanling.

sentences.zh: 膽氣過人，尤便弓馬。

translations.literal: His courage surpassed others; he was especially skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: His courage outmatched other men; bow and horse were his special arts.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始中，以軍功封晉安子。

translations.literal: During the Taishi era of Song he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jin'an for military merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Ming's Taishi reign he won enfeoffment as Viscount of Jin'an for military service.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，桂陽構難，盤龍時為冗從僕射，隨齊高帝頓新亭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui, when Guiyang raised trouble, Panlong was then Supernumerary Attendant of the Suite and followed Emperor Gao of Qi to encamp at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui year 2, when Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, Panlong was Supernumerary Attendant of the Suite and followed Emperor Gao to Xinting.

sentences.zh: 稍至驍騎將軍，改封沌陽侯。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General of Valiant Cavalry and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Chunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of Valiant Cavalry and was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Chunyang.

sentences.zh: 高帝即位，進號右將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao took the throne he was advanced to General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Panlong was promoted to General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，魏攻壽春，以盤龍為軍主、假節，助豫州刺史垣崇祖拒魏，大破之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan the Wei attacked Shouchun; Panlong was made army commander with acting staff and helped Inspector of Yu Province Yuan Chongzu resist the Wei, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 1 the Wei attacked Shouchun. Panlong was army commander with acting staff and, aiding Yuan Chongzu of Yu Province, crushed the invaders.

sentences.zh: 上聞之喜，下詔稱美，送金釵以二十枚與其愛妾杜氏。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he was pleased, issued an edict of praise, and sent twenty gold hairpins to his beloved concubine Lady Du.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejoiced, issued praise, and sent twenty gold hairpins to his favorite Lady Du.

sentences.zh: 手敕曰：「餉周公阿杜。

translations.literal: The imperial note said, "A gift for the Duke of Zhou's Lady Du."
translations.idiomatic: The note read, "For the Duke of Zhou's Lady Du."

sentences.zh: 」明年，魏攻淮陽，圍角城。

translations.literal: The next year the Wei attacked Huaiyang and besieged Jiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Wei struck Huaiyang and besieged Jiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，上遣軍主成買戍角城，辭于王儉曰：「今段之行，必以死報。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had sent the army commander Cheng Mai to garrison Jiaocheng; taking leave of Wang Jian he said, "This expedition of mine will surely be repaid with death."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had posted Cheng Mai at Jiaocheng. Leaving Wang Jian he said, "This march ends only in death."

sentences.zh: 衡門蓬戶，不朱斯白。

translations.literal: " A plain gate and thatched house need no vermilion to be white."
translations.idiomatic: A humble gate needs no paint to be white.

sentences.zh: 小人弱息當得一子。

translations.literal: " My young son ought to gain one son."
translations.idiomatic: " My young son should father a child."

sentences.zh: 」儉問其故，答曰：「若不殺賊，便為賊殺。

translations.literal: Jian asked the reason; he answered, "If I do not kill the enemy, I shall be killed by the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Jian asked why. He answered, "If I fail to kill the foe, the foe will kill me."

sentences.zh: 弱息不為世子，便為孝子；

translations.literal: " If the weak son is not heir, he will be a filial son;"
translations.idiomatic: " If the boy is not heir, let him be a filial mourner;"

sentences.zh: 孝子則門加素堊，世子則門施丹赭。

translations.literal: " a filial son then has white plaster on the gate; an heir has cinnabar and ochre on the gate."
translations.idiomatic: " the filial son whitewashes the gate; the heir paints it red."

sentences.zh: 」至是買被圍，上遣領軍將軍李安人救之，敕盤龍率馬步下淮陽就李安人。

translations.literal: By then Mai was besieged; the emperor sent General-in-Chief Li Anren to rescue him and ordered Panlong to lead horse and foot down from Huaiyang to join Li Anren.
translations.idiomatic: Mai was now besieged. The emperor sent Li Anren to relieve him and ordered Panlong down from Huaiyang with horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 買與魏拒戰，手所傷殺無數。

translations.literal: Mai fought the Wei in resistance and with his own hand killed countless men.
translations.idiomatic: Mai fought the Wei and killed countless men himself.

sentences.zh: 晨起手中忽有數升血，其日遂戰死。

translations.literal: At dawn several pints of blood suddenly appeared in his hands; that day he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn his hands filled with blood; that day he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 首見斬，猶屍據鞍奔還軍然後僵。

translations.literal: Though his head was cut off he still sat the saddle and galloped back to the army before stiffening.
translations.idiomatic: Beheaded, he still rode the saddle back to camp before he stiffened.

sentences.zh: 盤龍子奉叔單馬率二百餘人陷陣，魏軍萬餘騎張左右翼圍之。

translations.literal: Panlong's son Fengshu with a single horse led more than two hundred men into the formation; more than ten thousand Wei horsemen spread left and right wings to surround them.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong's son Fengshu charged in with one horse and two hundred men. Ten thousand Wei cavalry closed both wings around them.

sentences.zh: 一騎走還報奉叔已沒，盤龍方食，棄箸。

translations.literal: One rider ran back reporting Fengshu was lost; Panlong was at his meal and threw down his chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: A rider reported Fengshu was down. Panlong was eating and dropped his chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 馳馬奮矟，直奔魏陣，自稱「周公來」。

translations.literal: He spurred his horse, brandished his spear, and charged straight at the Wei formation, calling himself "the Duke of Zhou has come."
translations.idiomatic: He spurred forward, spear raised, crying, "The Duke of Zhou is here!"

sentences.zh: 魏人素畏盤龍驍名，莫不披靡。

translations.literal: The Wei people had long feared Panlong's fierce name and none did not scatter.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei had long feared Panlong's name; none stood firm.

sentences.zh: 時奉叔已大殺魏軍，得出在外，盤龍不知，乃東西觸擊，魏軍莫敢當，奉叔見其父久不出，復躍馬入陣，父子兩騎縈攪數萬人，魏軍大敗。

translations.literal: At that time Fengshu had already killed many Wei soldiers and got out beyond the formation; Panlong did not know this and struck east and west; the Wei army dared not oppose him; Fengshu saw his father had not emerged for long and again leaped his horse into the formation; father and son on two horses wheeled through tens of thousands of men; the Wei army suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu had already slaughtered deep in the enemy ranks and broken out. Panlong did not know it and struck left and right; the Wei dared not block him. Seeing his father linger, Fengshu charged back in. Father and son, two riders, whirled through tens of thousands until the Wei broke utterly.

sentences.zh: 盤龍父子由是名播北國。

translations.literal: Father and son thereby made their name known throughout the northern states.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son won fame across the northern realms.

sentences.zh: 形甚羸而臨軍勇果，諸將莫逮。

translations.literal: His form was very frail, yet facing the army he was brave and resolute; none of the generals could match him.
translations.idiomatic: He looked frail, yet in battle he was fierce; no general matched him.

sentences.zh: 永明五年，為大司馬，加征虜將軍、濟陽太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming he was made Grand Marshal, with the additional titles General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Administrator of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 5 he became Grand Marshal, with added rank as General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Administrator of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 武帝數講武，嘗令盤龍領馬軍，校騎騁矟。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu often held martial lectures and would have Panlong lead the cavalry, comparing horses in spear charges.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often held war games and had Panlong lead the horse corps in spear drills.

sentences.zh: 後以疾，為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later because of illness he was made Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Illness later made him Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 尋出為兗州刺史，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Inspector of Yan Province and was advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Yan Province and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 角城戍將張蒲與魏潛通，因大霧乘船入清中采樵，載魏人直向城東門，坐為有司所奏，詔白衣領職。

translations.literal: The garrison commander of Jiaocheng Zhang Pu had secret contact with Wei; taking advantage of heavy fog he took a boat into the Qing to gather firewood, loaded Wei men and went straight to the east gate of the city; he was impeached by the authorities and ordered to hold office in plain robes.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaocheng's commander Zhang Pu trafficked with Wei. In thick fog he rowed into the Qing to cut wood, ferried Wei soldiers to the east gate, and was denounced to serve in undress.

sentences.zh: 八坐尋奏重定，加領東平太守。

translations.literal: The Eight Seats soon memorialized to fix his status anew and added concurrent Administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Seats soon restored his rank and added Administrator of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 盤龍表年老才弱，不可鎮邊，求解職，見許。

translations.literal: Panlong memorialized that he was old and his talent weak and could not guard the frontier, requesting release from duty, which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong pleaded age and weakness unfit for the border; release was granted.

sentences.zh: 還為散騎常侍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On return he was made Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 武帝戲之曰：「卿著貂蟬，何如兜鍪？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu jested with him, saying, "You wear the cicada and fur finial—how does that compare to a helmet?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor teased him: "You wear court finery—how is that like a helm?"

sentences.zh: 」盤龍曰：「此貂蟬從兜鍪中生耳。

translations.literal: Panlong said, "This finery was born from the helmet."
translations.idiomatic: Panlong answered, "This finery grew out of the helmet."

sentences.zh: 」尋病卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: Soon he died of illness at age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 子奉叔，勇力絕人，少隨盤龍征討，所在暴掠。

translations.literal: His son Fengshu had strength surpassing others; from youth he followed Panlong on campaigns and wherever he went he plundered violently.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengshu possessed matchless strength. From youth he campaigned with Panlong and looted wherever he marched.

sentences.zh: 為東宮直合將軍。

translations.literal: He was Direct Guard General of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He became Direct Guard General of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 郁林在西州，奉叔密得自進，及即位，與直合將軍曹道剛為心膂。

translations.literal: When Yulin was in the Western Quarter, Fengshu secretly gained access to present himself; when Yulin took the throne he and Direct Guard General Cao Daogang became his inner confidants.
translations.idiomatic: While Yulin was heir in the Western Quarter, Fengshu found private access to him. On Yulin's accession he and Cao Daogang became the emperor's inner circle.

sentences.zh: 奉叔善騎馬，帝從其學騎，尤見親寵，得入內，無所忌憚。

translations.literal: Fengshu was skilled at riding horses; the emperor learned riding from him and favored him especially, gaining entry within the palace without restraint or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu rode superbly; the emperor learned horsemanship from him and favored him so that he entered the inner palace without restraint.

sentences.zh: 陵轢朝士，就司空王敬則換米二百斛，敬則以百斛與之，不受。

translations.literal: He bullied court gentlemen; he went to Minister of Works Wang Jingze to exchange for two hundred piculs of grain; Jingze gave him one hundred piculs and he would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: He bullied officials. Demanding two hundred piculs of grain from Wang Jingze, he refused the hundred piculs offered.

sentences.zh: 敬則大懼，乃更餉二百斛並金鉿等物。

translations.literal: Jingze was greatly afraid and therefore sent another two hundred piculs together with gold hairpins and other objects.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Jingze sent another two hundred piculs plus gold hairpins and gifts.

sentences.zh: 敬則有一內妓，帝令奉叔求。

translations.literal: Jingze had a palace concubine; the emperor ordered Fengshu to demand her.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze kept a palace woman; the emperor ordered Fengshu to take her.

sentences.zh: 奉叔不通徑前，從者執單刀皆半拔，敬則跣走入內。

translations.literal: Fengshu would not go by the proper path; his followers drew single blades half unsheathed; Jingze ran in barefoot into the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu stormed in without ceremony, followers' blades half drawn. Jingze fled barefoot indoors.

sentences.zh: 既而自計不免，乃出，遙呼奉叔曰：「弟那忽能顧？

translations.literal: Then calculating he could not escape, he came out and called from afar to Fengshu, "Younger brother, how could you suddenly turn on me?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing escape impossible, he came out and called, "Brother, how can you treat me so?"

sentences.zh: 」奉叔宣旨求妓意，乃得釋。

translations.literal: Fengshu announced the imperial intent seeking the concubine, and only then was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu stated the imperial demand for the woman, and Jingze was spared.

sentences.zh: 與綦母珍、曹道剛、朱隆之共相唇齒，煽弄威權。

translations.literal: With Qi Mu Zhen, Cao Daogang, and Zhu Longzhi they were like lips and teeth, fanning and wielding authority.
translations.idiomatic: With Qi Mu Zhen, Cao Daogang, and Zhu Longzhi he formed a clique that twisted power at will.

sentences.zh: 奉叔常翼單刀二十口，出入禁闈，既無別詔，門衛莫敢訶。

translations.literal: Fengshu commonly carried twenty single blades at his side entering and leaving the forbidden gates; as there was no separate edict, the gate guards dared not challenge him.
translations.idiomatic: He routinely carried twenty swords through the forbidden gates; without a special edict guards dared not stop him.

sentences.zh: 每語人云：「周郎刀不識君。

translations.literal: He often told people, "Young Zhou's blade does not know you."
translations.idiomatic: He would say, "Young Zhou's blade knows no master but me."

sentences.zh: 」求武帝御角及輿，並求禦仗以給左右。

translations.literal: He sought the emperor's horn bow and carriage and also sought imperial arms to supply his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded the emperor's horn bow, carriage, and imperial arms for his men.

sentences.zh: 事無不從。

translations.literal: In affairs nothing was refused him.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing was refused.

sentences.zh: 又求黃門郎，明帝作輔，固執不能得，乃令蕭諶、蕭坦之說帝出奉叔為外鎮，樹腹心。

translations.literal: He also sought the post of Palace Attendant; when Emperor Ming was regent he firmly would not grant it; then he had Xiao Chen and Xiao Tanzhi persuade the emperor to send Fengshu out to a frontier command and plant a trusted man in his place.
translations.idiomatic: He sought Palace Attendant rank; regent Emperor Ming refused. Xiao Chen and Xiao Tanzhi then persuaded the emperor to post Fengshu abroad and plant a loyal man within.

sentences.zh: 又說奉叔以方伯之重，奉叔納其言。

translations.literal: They also persuaded Fengshu with the weight of a regional command; Fengshu accepted their words.
translations.idiomatic: They flattered him with a provincial command; he agreed.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，出為青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he went out as Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year 1 he was sent out as Inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 奉叔就帝求千戶侯，帝許之。

translations.literal: Fengshu asked the emperor for a marquisate of one thousand households; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the throne for a thousand-household marquisate; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 明帝以為不可。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming thought it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming objected.

sentences.zh: 忽謂蕭諶曰：「若不能見與千戶侯，不復應減五百戶；

translations.literal: Suddenly he said to Xiao Chen, "If you cannot give me a thousand-household marquisate, I will not accept even five hundred households being reduced;"
translations.idiomatic: He told Xiao Chen sharply, "Deny me a thousand-household marquis and I will not take five hundred less either;"

sentences.zh: 不爾，周郎當就刀頭取辦耳。

translations.literal: otherwise Young Zhou will settle the matter at the blade's point."
translations.idiomatic: or Young Zhou will settle it at sword point."

sentences.zh: 」既而封曲江縣男，奉叔大怒，於眾中攘刀，厲目切齒。

translations.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Qujiang; Fengshu was furious and in the crowd brandished his blade, glaring and grinding his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: He was given only Viscount of Qujiang. Fengshu raged, drew his blade in the assembly, glaring and gnashing his teeth.

sentences.zh: 明帝說諭乃受。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming persuaded and instructed him and only then did he accept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming talked him down before he accepted.

sentences.zh: 及將之鎮，明帝慮其不可復製，因其早入，引往後堂，執送廷尉盡之。

translations.literal: When he was about to go to his command, Emperor Ming feared he could not be controlled again; because he entered early, he was led to the rear hall, seized, and sent to the Minister of Justice, where he was executed to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, Emperor Ming feared losing control. Lured early to the rear hall, he was seized and executed to the last man at court.

sentences.zh: 王廣之

translations.literal: Wang Guangzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangzhi

sentences.zh: 王廣之字士林，一字林之，沛郡相人也。

translations.literal: Wang Guangzhi, style Shilin, also styled Linzhi, was a native of Xiang in Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangzhi, courtesy names Shilin and Linzhi, came from Xiang in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好弓馬，便捷有勇力。

translations.literal: From youth he loved bow and horse; he was nimble and possessed courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved bow and horse, was quick, brave, and strong.

sentences.zh: 初為馬隊主，隨劉勉征殷琰。

translations.literal: At first he was chief of a horse detachment and followed Liu Mian in campaigning against Yin Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He began as horse detachment chief under Liu Mian against Yin Yan.

sentences.zh: 兵既盛而合肥戍又阻兵為寇。

translations.literal: The army was already strong yet the Hefei garrison also blocked the army as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The army was strong, but the Hefei garrison also blocked them as enemies.

sentences.zh: 勉宣令軍中求征合肥者，以大郡賞之。

translations.literal: Mian proclaimed throughout the army seeking one to campaign against Hefei, with a great commandery as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Mian called for volunteers to take Hefei, promising a great commandery as prize.

sentences.zh: 廣之曰：「若得將軍所乘馬，判能制之。

translations.literal: Guangzhi said, "If I obtain the general's own mount, I can surely subdue it."
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi said, "Give me the general's own horse and I will take it."

sentences.zh: 」勉幢主皇甫肅謂勉曰：「廣之敢奪節下馬，可斬。

translations.literal: Mian's banner chief Huangfu Su said to Mian, "Guangzhi dares seize my lord's horse—he should be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Mian's banner chief Huangfu Su said, "Guangzhi dares seize your horse—cut him down."

sentences.zh: 」勉曰：「觀其意必能立功。

translations.literal: Mian said, "Judging his intent he will surely be able to achieve merit."
translations.idiomatic: Mian said, "He means to win glory—let him try."

sentences.zh: 」即推鞍下馬與之。

translations.literal: He immediately pushed off the saddle and dismounted, giving the horse to him.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted and gave him the horse.

sentences.zh: 及行，合肥果拔，勉大賞之，即擢為軍主。

translations.literal: When they marched, Hefei was indeed taken; Mian greatly rewarded him and immediately promoted him to army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Hefei fell. Mian richly rewarded him and made him army commander at once.

sentences.zh: 廣之於勉前謂肅曰：「節下若從卿言，非唯斬壯士，亦自無以平賊。

translations.literal: Before Mian, Guangzhi said to Su, "If my lord had followed your advice, he would not only have beheaded a stalwart but also himself have had no means to pacify the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Before Mian, Guangzhi told Su, "Had your lord listened to you, he would have killed a hero and never pacified the enemy."

sentences.zh: 卿不賞才乃至此邪！

translations.literal: You do not reward talent and have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: You cannot recognize talent—that is your fault!"

sentences.zh: 」廣之由此知名。

translations.literal: Guangzhi thereby became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From this Guangzhi became famous.

sentences.zh: 初封蒲圻子。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Puqi.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed Viscount of Puqi.

sentences.zh: 肅有學術，善舉止，廣之亦雅相推慕。

translations.literal: Su had learning and fine deportment; Guangzhi also in refined fashion admired and looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Su was learned and graceful; Guangzhi admired him sincerely.

sentences.zh: 勉亡後，肅更依廣之，廣之盛相賞接，啟武帝以為東海太守，不念舊惡如此。

translations.literal: After Mian died, Su again relied on Guangzhi; Guangzhi greatly favored and received him and reported to Emperor Wu to make him Administrator of Donghai—so little did he bear old grudges.
translations.idiomatic: After Mian's death Su clung to Guangzhi, who favored him and recommended him to Emperor Wu as Administrator of Donghai—forgetting old quarrels.

sentences.zh: 廣之後以征伐功，位給事中、冠軍將軍，改封寧都縣子。

translations.literal: Later Guangzhi for campaign merit held the post of Gentleman of the Palace and General Who Vanquishes Champions and his enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: For campaigns he became Gentleman of the Palace and General Who Vanquishes Champions, re-enfeoffed Viscount of Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝廢蒼梧，出廣之為徐州刺史、鍾離太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi deposed the Cangwu emperor, he sent Guangzhi out as Inspector of Xu Province and Administrator of Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao deposed the Cangwu emperor, Guangzhi was sent as Inspector of Xu and Administrator of Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，廣之留都下，豫平石頭，仍從高帝頓新亭。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, Guangzhi remained in the capital, took part in pacifying Stone City, and still followed Emperor Gao to encamp at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Guangzhi stayed in the capital, helped take Stone City, and followed Emperor Gao to Xinting.

sentences.zh: 高帝誅黃回，回弟駟及從弟馬、兄子奴亡逸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao executed Huang Hui, Hui's younger brother Si and cousin Ma and elder brother's son Nu fled and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Hui was executed, his brother Si, cousin Ma, and nephew Nu fled.

sentences.zh: 高帝與廣之書曰：「黃回雖有微勳，而罪過轉不可容。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao wrote to Guangzhi, "Huang Hui though he had slight merit, his crimes in the end could not be tolerated."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao wrote Guangzhi: "Huang Hui's small merits could not balance his crimes."

sentences.zh: 近遂啟請禦大小二輿為刺史服飾，吾乃不惜為其啟聞，政恐得輿復求畫輪車。

translations.literal: Recently he even requested the great and small imperial carriages for inspector's regalia; I was not unwilling to report it for him, but only feared that obtaining the carriage he would again request a painted-wheel carriage."
translations.idiomatic: He lately asked for imperial carriages fit for an inspector; I would have reported it, fearing he would next demand a painted imperial coach."

sentences.zh: 此外罪不可勝數，弟自悉之。

translations.literal: Beyond this his crimes are beyond counting—you yourself know them."
translations.idiomatic: His other crimes are countless—you know them."

sentences.zh: 今啟依法。

translations.literal: Now I report according to law."
translations.idiomatic: Execute the law now."

sentences.zh: 」令廣之於江西搜捕駟等。

translations.literal: He ordered Guangzhi to search west of the river and capture Si and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Guangzhi to hunt Si and the rest west of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 子珍國字德重，仕齊為南譙太守，有能名。

translations.literal: His son Zhenguo, style Dezhong, served Qi as Administrator of Nanqiao and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhenguo, courtesy name Dezhong, served Qi as Administrator of Nanqiao with a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 時郡境苦饑，乃發米散財以振窮乏。

translations.literal: At that time the commandery suffered bitter famine; he therefore distributed grain and scattered wealth to relieve the poor and destitute.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was starving; he issued grain and cash to save the destitute.

sentences.zh: 高帝手敕云：「卿愛人活國，甚副吾意。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gao wrote in his own hand, "You love the people and give life to the state—very much in accord with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao wrote by hand, "You cherish the people—exactly what I wished."

sentences.zh: 永明初，遷桂陽內史，討捕賊盜，境內肅清。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming he was transferred to Interior Administrator of Guiyang, pursued and captured bandits and robbers, and within the borders was cleared and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongming he governed Guiyang, crushed bandits, and cleared the region.

sentences.zh: 罷任還都，路經江州，刺史柳世隆臨渚餞別，見珍國還裝輕素，歎曰：「此真良二千石也，」還為大司馬中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Leaving office and returning to the capital, his route passed Jiang Province; Inspector Liu Shilong came to the ford to bid farewell; seeing Zhenguo's return baggage light and plain, he sighed and said, "This is truly a good two-thousand-dan official," and on return he was made Major in the Grand Marshal's central army.
