translations.idiomatic: Returning to court via Jiang Province, Liu Shilong saw his light baggage and sighed, "A true two-thousand-dan official," then named him Major under the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 武帝雅相知賞，謂其父廣之曰：「珍國應堪大用，卿可謂老蚌也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu in refined fashion knew and appreciated him and said to his father Guangzhi, "Zhenguo should be fit for great employment—you may be called an old oyster."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu prized him and told Guangzhi, "Zhenguo deserves high office—you are the old oyster that bore the pearl."

sentences.zh: 」廣之曰：「臣不敢辭。

translations.literal: Guangzhi said, "Your servant dares not decline."
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi said, "I dare not refuse the praise."

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 帝每歎曰：「晚代將家子弟如珍國者少矣。

translations.literal: The emperor often sighed, "In this late age there are few sons of general's houses like Zhenguo."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Few sons of generals in this age match Zhenguo."

sentences.zh: 」累遷遊擊將軍，父憂去職。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General Who Roams in Attack and left office for his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Roams in Attack, then left for mourning his father.

sentences.zh: 建武末，魏軍圍司州，明帝使徐州刺史裴叔業攻拔渦陽，以為聲援，起珍國為輔國將軍助焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianwu the Wei army besieged Si Province; Emperor Ming sent Inspector of Xu Province Pei Shuye to attack and take Woyang as a supporting thrust and raised Zhenguo as General Who Assists the State to help.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianwu the Wei besieged Si Province. Pei Shuye of Xu was sent to take Woyang; Zhenguo was made acting General Who Assists the State to aid him.

sentences.zh: 魏將楊大眼大眾奄至，叔業懼，棄軍走。

translations.literal: The Wei commander Yang Dayan came with a great host in sudden arrival; Shuye was afraid and abandoned the army and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei commander Yang Dayan swept in with a huge force. Shuye panicked and fled.

sentences.zh: 珍國率其眾殿，故不至大敗。

translations.literal: Zhenguo led his troops as rearguard, and therefore they did not suffer great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguo covered the retreat and kept the army from ruin.

sentences.zh: 及會稽太守王敬則反，珍國又率眾拒之。

translations.literal: When Administrator of Kuaiji Wang Jingze rebelled, Zhenguo again led troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingze of Kuaiji rebelled, Zhenguo led troops against him.

sentences.zh: 永元中，為北徐州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: During the Yongyuan era he was Inspector of North Xu Province, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan he was Inspector of North Xu, rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 梁武起兵，東昏召珍國以眾還都，使出屯朱雀門，為王茂所敗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops, Emperor Donghun summoned Zhenguo with his forces back to the capital, ordered him out to garrison the Vermilion Bird Gate, and he was defeated by Wang Mao.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang forces rose, Donghun recalled Zhenguo to garrison the Vermilion Bird Gate; Wang Mao defeated him.

sentences.zh: 乃入城，密遣郗纂奉明鏡獻誠于梁武帝，帝斷金以報之。

translations.literal: He then entered the city and secretly sent Chi Zuan to present a bright mirror in pledge of loyalty to Emperor Wu of Liang; the emperor broke gold to reply.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the city and secretly sent Chi Zuan with a bright mirror pledging loyalty to Liang; the emperor broke gold in reply.

sentences.zh: 時侍中、衛尉張稷都督眾軍，珍國潛結稷腹心張齊要稷，稷許之。

translations.literal: At that time Attendant-in-Chief and Commandant of the Guard Zhang Ji commanded the armies; Zhenguo secretly joined with Ji's trusted man Zhang Qi to win Ji; Ji consented.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Zhang Ji commanded the armies. Zhenguo won Zhang Qi, Ji's confidant, to a plot; Ji agreed.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅旦，珍國引稷于衛尉府勒兵入自雲龍門，殺東昏於內殿，與稷會尚書僕射王亮等於西鍾下，使國子博士范雲等奉東昏首歸梁武。

translations.literal: On the morning of the bingyin day of the twelfth month Zhenguo led Ji with troops from the Commandant of the Guard's office to enter through the Cloud Dragon Gate and killed Donghun in the inner hall; with Ji he met Minister of Works Wang Liang and others below the western bell tower and had the Doctor of the National University Fan Yun and others present Donghun's head to Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth month, bingyin morning, Zhenguo led Ji's troops through the Cloud Dragon Gate, killed Donghun in the inner hall, met Wang Liang below the western bell tower, and sent Fan Yun with Donghun's head to Liang.

sentences.zh: 後因侍宴，帝曰：「卿明鏡尚存，昔金何在？

translations.literal: Later at a banquet attendance the emperor said, "Your bright mirror still exists—where is the former gold?"
translations.idiomatic: Later at court the emperor said, "Your mirror still shines—where is my gold?"

sentences.zh: 」珍國曰：「黃金謹在臣肘，不敢失墜。

translations.literal: Zhenguo said, "The yellow gold is carefully at my elbow; I dare not let it fall."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguo answered, "The gold is safe on my arm—I have not dropped it."

sentences.zh: 」歷位左衛將軍，加散騎常侍，封灄陽侯。

translations.literal: He held posts in succession as Left Guard General, with additional Regular Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Tanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Left Guard General, Regular Attendant, and Marquis of Tanyang.

sentences.zh: 遷都官尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Court for the Nobility.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of the Court for the Nobility.

sentences.zh: 初，珍國自以廢殺東昏，意望台鼎。

translations.literal: At first Zhenguo because he himself had deposed and killed Donghun expected the pinnacle of office.
translations.idiomatic: At first he expected the highest office for killing Donghun.

sentences.zh: 先是出為梁、秦二州刺史，心常鬱怏，酒後於坐啟云：「臣近入梁山便哭。

translations.literal: Earlier he had gone out as Inspector of Liang and Qin provinces; his heart was always sullen; drunk at his seat he reported, "Your servant lately entered Liang Mountain and wept."
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Liang and Qin, he brooded; drunk at court he said, "I wept on Liang Mountain."

sentences.zh: 」帝大驚曰：「卿若哭東昏則已晚，若哭我，我復未死。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly startled and said, "If you weep for Donghun it is already late; if you weep for me, I am not yet dead."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started. "Weep for Donghun and it is too late; weep for me and I am not dead yet."

sentences.zh: 」珍國起拜謝，竟不答，坐即散，因此疏退，久方有此進。

translations.literal: Zhenguo rose and bowed in thanks but in the end did not answer; the seating immediately dispersed; because of this he was kept at a distance and only after long time received this advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed but would not explain; the feast broke up; he fell from favor and only slowly rose again.

sentences.zh: 天監五年，魏任城王澄攻鍾離，帝遣珍國為援，因問討賊方略。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianjian Prince Cheng of Rencheng of Wei attacked Zhongli; the emperor sent Zhenguo as relief and asked him the strategy for defeating the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 5 Wei's Prince Cheng besieged Zhongli. Zhenguo was sent as relief and asked for strategy.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣常患魏眾少，不苦其多。

translations.literal: He answered, "Your servant always worries that the Wei host is too few, not that they are too many."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I never fear too many Wei—I fear too few."

sentences.zh: 」武帝壯其言，乃假節與眾軍同赴。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu admired his words and therefore gave him acting staff to go with the armies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired this and gave him acting staff to join the host.

sentences.zh: 魏軍退，班師。

translations.literal: The Wei army retreated and the army returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei withdrew; the army marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 又出為南秦、梁二州刺史，會梁州長史夏侯道遷以州降魏，珍國步道出魏興，將襲之，不果，遂留鎮焉。

translations.literal: He again went out as Inspector of South Qin and Liang provinces; when the Chief Administrator of Liang Province Xia Hou Daoqian surrendered the province to Wei, Zhenguo went on foot from Weixing intending to strike him, did not succeed, and therefore remained on garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to South Qin and Liang. When Liang's chief administrator Xia Hou Daoqian defected to Wei, Zhenguo marched from Weixing to strike him, failed, and stayed to garrison.

sentences.zh: 改封宜陽縣侯，累遷丹陽尹。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Yiyang and he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Re-enfeoffed Marquis of Yiyang, he rose to Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈車騎將軍，諡曰威。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made General of the Chariots and Cavalry with the posthumous title Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died, posthumously General of the Chariots and Cavalry, titled Wei.

sentences.zh: 子僧度嗣。

translations.literal: His son Sengdu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sengdu inherited.

sentences.zh: 張齊字子向，馮翊郡人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi, style Zixiang, was a man of Fengyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi, courtesy name Zixiang, came from Fengyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 少有膽氣。

translations.literal: From youth he had courage and mettle.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and spirited.

sentences.zh: 初事荊州司馬垣曆生，曆生酗酒，遇下嚴酷，不禮之。

translations.literal: At first he served the Jing Province Staff Major Yuan Lisheng; Lisheng was addicted to wine and toward subordinates harsh and cruel, showing him no courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Jing Province Staff Major Yuan Lisheng, a drunkard who treated subordinates harshly and scorned Qi.

sentences.zh: 及吳郡張稷為荊府司馬，齊復從之，甚見重，以為腹心。

translations.literal: When Zhang Ji of Wu commandery became Jing headquarters Staff Major, Qi again followed him and was greatly valued, taken as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Ji of Wu became Jing staff major, Qi followed him, won deep trust, and became his confidant.

sentences.zh: 齊盡心事稷，稷為南兗州，擢為府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Qi devoted himself wholly to Ji; when Ji was in South Yan Province, he was promoted to Central Army Attendant in the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Qi served Ji wholeheartedly; when Ji held South Yan, Qi was raised to headquarters Central Army Attendant.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝起兵，東昏征稷歸，都督宮城諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops, Emperor Donghun summoned Ji back and made him commander-in-chief of palace city military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang forces rose, Donghun recalled Ji to command the palace defenses.

sentences.zh: 齊夜引珍國就稷，齊手自執燭定謀。

translations.literal: At night Qi led Zhenguo to Ji; Qi himself held the candle to fix the plot.
translations.idiomatic: At night Qi brought Zhenguo to Ji and held the candle while they fixed the plot.

sentences.zh: 明旦與稷、珍國即東昏於殿內，齊手殺焉。

translations.literal: At dawn together with Ji and Zhenguo they faced Donghun in the hall and Qi with his own hand killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he, Ji, and Zhenguo confronted Donghun in the hall; Qi killed him with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封齊安昌侯，位曆陽太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, Qi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anchang and made Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang emperor took the throne, Qi was enfeoffed Marquis of Anchang and made Administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 齊手不知書，目不識字，在郡清整，吏事甚修。

translations.literal: Qi by hand did not know writing and by eye did not recognize characters; in the commandery he was pure and orderly and official business was thoroughly conducted.
translations.idiomatic: Qi could neither write nor read; yet in office he was scrupulous and ran affairs well.

sentences.zh: 天監四年，魏將王足攻蜀，圍巴西，帝以齊為輔國將軍救蜀，未至，足退。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian the Wei general Wang Zu attacked Shu and besieged Brazil; the emperor made Qi General Who Assists the State to rescue Shu; before he arrived, Zu retreated.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 4 Wei general Wang Zu besieged Brazil in Shu. Qi was sent to relieve Shu; before he arrived, Zu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 齊進戍南安，遷巴西太守。

translations.literal: Qi advanced to garrison Nan'an and was transferred to Administrator of Brazil.
translations.idiomatic: Qi advanced to garrison Nan'an and was made Administrator of Brazil.

sentences.zh: 初，南鄭沒于魏，乃於益州西置南梁州。

translations.literal: At first Nanzheng had fallen to Wei; therefore South Liang Province was established west of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanzheng fell to Wei, the court set up South Liang Province west of Yi.

sentences.zh: 州鎮草創，皆仰益州取足。

translations.literal: The provincial garrison was newly founded and all depended on Yi Province for full supply.
translations.idiomatic: The new provincial seat depended entirely on Yi for supplies.

sentences.zh: 齊上夷獠義租，得米二十萬斛。

translations.literal: Qi reported righteous tribute from the Yi and Liao peoples and obtained two hundred thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Qi levied righteous tribute from the Yi and Liao and gathered two hundred thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進假節，督益州外水諸軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was advanced with acting staff as overseer of all armies outside the waters of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he received acting staff to command armies beyond Yi's river line.

sentences.zh: 齊在益部累年，討擊蠻獠，身無寧歲。

translations.literal: Qi in the Yi region for accumulated years pursued and attacked the Man and Liao; he himself had no year of peace.
translations.idiomatic: For years in the southwest he fought Man and Liao without a peaceful year.

sentences.zh: 其居軍中，能身親勞辱，與士卒同勤苦，自頓舍城壘皆委曲得其便。

translations.literal: In camp he could personally share labor and hardship with the soldiers in toil; from his own quarters to city ramparts he arranged everything for their convenience.
translations.idiomatic: In camp he shared soldiers' labor, arranging quarters and walls for their comfort.

sentences.zh: 調給衣糧資用，人無困乏。

translations.literal: He regulated and supplied clothing, grain, and funds so that men were without want or shortage.
translations.idiomatic: He supplied clothing, grain, and pay so none went wanting.

sentences.zh: 既為物情所歸，蠻獠亦不敢犯，是以威名行於庸蜀。

translations.literal: Since he was what sentiment turned to, the Man and Liao also did not dare offend him; therefore his awe-inspiring name extended through Yong and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Men and tribes alike respected him; even Man and Liao dared not offend. His fame spread through Yong and Shu.

sentences.zh: 巴西郡居益州之半，又當東道沖要，刺史經過，軍府遠涉多窮匱。

translations.literal: Brazil commandery occupied half of Yi Province and also lay on the vital eastern route; when inspectors passed through, the army headquarters on long journeys were often impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: Brazil held half of Yi and sat on the eastern thoroughfare; passing inspectors and distant headquarters often went broke on the road.

sentences.zh: 齊緣路聚糧食，種蔬菜，行者皆取給焉。

translations.literal: Qi along the route gathered grain and food and planted vegetables; travelers all obtained supplies from him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi stocked grain along the route and planted vegetables so every traveler was fed.

sentences.zh: 曆南梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Inspector of South Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Inspector of South Liang.

sentences.zh: 遷信武將軍、征西鄱陽王司馬、新興永甯二郡太守，未發卒，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Trustworthy Martial General, Staff Major to the Western Campaign Prince of Poyang, and Administrator of the two commanderies Xinxing and Yongning; before he set out he died and received the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Trustworthy Martial General and Staff Major to the Prince of Poyang on the western campaign, and Administrator of Xinxing and Yongning; he died before departing and was posthumously titled Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋氏將季，亂離日兆，家懷逐鹿，人有異圖。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When the Song house neared its end, disorder and separation daily portended; every household harbored the intent to contend for the realm and every man had a different design.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: As Song neared collapse, chaos loomed daily; households dreamed of empire and men plotted divergent courses.

sentences.zh: 高帝觀釁深視，將符興運。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao observed the openings with deep vision and was about to grasp the mandate of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao read the moment with sharp eyes and seized the turning fortune.

sentences.zh: 李安人、戴僧靜、桓康、焦度、曹武、呂安國、周山圖、周盤龍、王廣之等，或早見誠款，或備盡心力，或受委方面，或功成麾下，其所以自致榮寵，夫豈徒然，蓋亦驗人心之有歸，樂推之非妄也。

translations.literal: Li Anren, Dai Sengjing, Huan Kang, Jiao Du, Cao Wu, Lu Anguo, Zhou Shantu, Zhou Panlong, Wang Guangzhi, and the others—some early showed sincere allegiance, some exhausted heart and strength, some received commission on the frontier, some achieved merit under his banner—the means by which they themselves attained glory and favor were surely not in vain; it also verified that hearts had a place to turn and that willing elevation was no delusion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Anren, Dai Sengjing, Huan Kang, Jiao Du, Cao Wu, Lu Anguo, Zhou Shantu, Zhou Panlong, Wang Guangzhi, and others—some pledged early, some gave everything, some held the frontiers, some won battles at his side—their honors were earned, not accidental. They proved that loyalty could find its lord and that merit would be recognized.

sentences.zh: 語云：「勇而無禮則亂。

translations.literal: The saying goes, "Courage without propriety becomes disorder."
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says, "Courage without ritual breeds chaos."

sentences.zh: 」觀夫奉叔取進之道，不亦幾於亂乎。

translations.literal: Considering Fengshu's way of demanding advancement, did it not nearly reach disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu's path to power was chaos itself.

sentences.zh: 其致屠戮，亦其宜矣。

translations.literal: That he met slaughter was also fitting.
translations.idiomatic: His execution was only just.

sentences.zh: 珍國明鏡雖在，而斷金莫驗，報罵之義，理則宜然，台輔之冀，其何爽也。

translations.literal: Though Zhenguo's bright mirror still existed, the broken gold was not verified; the meaning of repaying abuse in kind was right in principle, yet the hope for the pinnacle of office—how was it missed?
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguo kept his mirror, yet the broken gold pledge went unrewarded in full. Gratitude demanded repayment, yet the highest office he hoped for never came.

sentences.zh: 張齊人位本下，志望易充，績宣所蒞，其殆優也。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi's person and rank were originally low; his ambitions were easily satisfied; the achievements and governance he reached were perhaps superior.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi rose from low rank with modest desires; what he achieved in office may have been the finest of them all.
